findings.title: Second `self.downsize` overrides the first and breaks `Jobs::ResizeEmoji`
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so only `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` exists, and the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` form is dead code. `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`. That is 5 arguments against a maximum of 4, so it raises `ArgumentError`. The emoji resize job then fails for every uploaded emoji and the oversize check is never done. Fix it by keeping both call forms. For example, have the controller call `downsize(path, path, "80%", "", ...)`, or have the emoji job pass `"100x100"` and delete the width/height overload. Also add a spec for the new form and one for the emoji job.

findings.title: Percentage downsizing is wrong for animated GIFs and the loop can silently do nothing
findings.body: With `allow_animation` on and a path ending in `.gif`, `optimize` picks `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:115-124`). `--resize-fit` takes `WxH`, not a percentage, so gifsicle should fail and `convert_with` returns false. The result is ignored, so all 5 attempts are spent on a file that never shrinks. The upload then fails the size validator with no hint that downsizing was tried. In the other case, where the path has no `.gif` extension (Rack multipart temp files normally have none, which I did not confirm), `downsize_instructions` reads `#{from}[0]` and writes the first frame only. That flattens an animated GIF into a still image without telling the user. The return value of `downsize` should be checked, and the loop should stop when it returns false. GIF handling needs an explicit decision, either skipping animated GIFs or using a gifsicle-compatible scale option.

findings.title: Client-side size limits hard-coded to 10 MB for all file types
findings.body: Line 182 now ignores both `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. Attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 1024 in the test helper) and 10 MB now pass the client check, upload in full, and are only rejected by `UploadValidator#maximum_file_size` (`lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:80-87`). The user sees the error after the upload finishes. Images above 10 MB are blocked client-side even if an admin set `max_image_size_kb` higher, and the dialog reports a limit of 10240 kB that matches no setting. Keep the per-type setting for attachments, and use `Math.max(max_image_size_kb, 10 * 1024)` or similar for images. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hard-coded value. The existing JS test `prevents files that are too big from being uploaded` (`test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61`) sets `max_image_size_kb = 5` and uploads a 10 KB image, expecting `file_too_large` with `max_size_kb: 5`. It will now fail because 10 KB < 10 MB, and it needs updating.

findings.title: Magic 10 MB limit duplicated between server and client with no setting
findings.body: The 10 MB cap appears as `10.megabytes` here and as `10 * 1024` twice in `utilities.js` (lines 182 and 246). The server-side upload path has no equivalent cap, so it is enforced only by the web server. Consider a single constant or site setting so the values cannot drift apart.

contracts.failure_mode: downsize returns false on a convert/gifsicle failure and the result is ignored. The loop then runs 5 times without effect and ends in the generic too-large error. Animated GIFs are the likely trigger.

contracts.before_after: Before, downsize(from,to,w,h,opts) worked. After, the duplicate definition at line 149 replaces it, so the emoji job's 5-argument call raises ArgumentError. resize keeps its signature.
contracts.visible_effect: Emoji uploads are no longer downsized to 100x100, and the job fails in the background.
contracts.failure_mode: ArgumentError raised in Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute. Sidekiq retries and then fails.

contracts.action: Hard-code 10 MB client-side validation and 413 message

contracts.before_after: Before: the per-type site setting was checked before upload. After: a fixed 10 MB check, so attachment limits are enforced only server-side.

summary: The PR adds auto-downsizing of oversize images and hard-codes a 10 MB limit client-side. I found one blocker: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice, and the second definition removes the `(max_width, max_height)` form, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` now raises ArgumentError. I also found a bug in the animated GIF path, which can silently fail or flatten the image. The client-side hard-coding of 10 MB drops the per-type limit settings and breaks an existing JS test.
